restaurant_name: คลินิกทันตกรรม เด็นทอลโฟกัส เครือสหพัฒน์
text:
Before having my upper and lower wisdom teeth extracted, I had an appointment a week later to have the stitches removed and two more fillings done. My appointment was at 11 am, but the doctor was busy with another patient, so I waited 15-20 minutes. Another patient who arrived after me was served first. I waited until noon to see the doctor. The stitch removal took less than a minute, and they said it was done. I asked about the fillings, and the doctor said I hadn't scheduled them. I was confused; I didn't get any fillings after waiting for a full hour. I felt disappointed. Why did they let someone who came after me go first when stitch removal only takes less than a minute? My appointment was at 11 am, but I got served at noon.
The doctor also spoke curtly, as if they didn't want to do the work.
I paid for the treatment; I wasn't asking for free service and didn't use any benefits.
I understand the doctor might have many patients and couldn't pay attention to just one person like me.
I gave 1 star.
I didn't really want to give any stars, but I can't post without giving stars.

restaurant_name: คลินิกทันตกรรม เด็นทอลโฟกัส เครือสหพัฒน์
text:
This review is based on my own personal experience and does not necessarily reflect everyone.
From reading previous reviews, I suspect it's the same doctor, as their situation was similar to mine. I wanted to share this information with those who are considering a move.

I moved from Chonburi to Bangkok, but I return regularly for follow-up appointments, about every other month.

Later, the doctor suggested a move to Bangkok, but his tone and manner of speaking were harsh and somewhat sarcastic. This made me feel disrespected as a patient. However, my case was nearing completion, and I'd been working on it for almost two and a half years, so I was determined to finish it at the same location first. Since then, we've been trying every month.

For my last appointment, I drove all the way from Bangkok to Chonburi, but I wasn't able to get the tooth extracted as planned because I had other business to attend. I asked for a replacement braces first, but the doctor said I needed to have the tooth extracted as well or else I'd have to reschedule. His tone and manner of speaking made me feel very uncomfortable and pressured, as I was already there and unable to adjust my treatment plan to the situation.

In the end, the doctor agreed to just a replacement braces, but the conversation didn't make me feel very understood about travel convenience. The round-trip distance was quite far for me.

I understand that this treatment might be suitable for some people. But for us, we felt it didn't meet our needs regarding flexibility in terms of time and communication.
Finally, we decided to move the case back to Bangkok because we felt uncomfortable almost every time we had to go to the dentist.

restaurant_name: คลินิกทันตกรรม เด็นทอลโฟกัส เครือสหพัฒน์
text:
We had an appointment to adjust our equipment and were 10 minutes late. We informed the counter staff that we were 10 minutes late, but they didn't say anything and just told us to wait. One person was served before us. After that person left, we still hadn't been allowed in, and we waited for about half an hour. So we asked what time we could be seen.

The counter staff said, "The doctor is on a lunch break. Would you like to wait? If not, please reschedule for another day because you are late."

We then asked, "What time would we have to wait?" (Thinking to ourselves, "Okay, I'll just buy something nearby and come back later.")

The staff replied, "I can't answer that. If you're not comfortable waiting, please reschedule for another day because you are late."

We then said, "Why didn't you tell us that earlier? We wouldn't have had to wait."

The staff just gave us an indifferent look and told us to reschedule. They didn't apologize. But when we paid after the procedure, they were so polite; it was like a different person altogether.

Okay, we understand we were 10 minutes late, but they just wouldn't let us in after that person left. We were confused. If they were going to eat, why didn't they tell us we had to wait? They could have just said so. But they made us sit and wait all alone, with no one else around, and they didn't even bother to tell us what to do unless we asked. They couldn't even tell us how long they would be eating. I'm confused. What kind of service is this? Or if we were late and they weren't going to serve us, they could have told us when we arrived. We could have accepted that, just let us know. Instead, they made us sit and wait for the doctor to finish eating without even telling us they were eating and asking if we wanted to wait. I'm very confused. Here's what I think is unacceptable:
1. We were 10 minutes late. If it wasn't convenient to change the orthodontic rubber bands, they should have informed us that we had to arrive on time.
2. They made us sit and wait for half an hour without saying a word about waiting for the doctor to finish eating before they would serve us. We had to get up and ask ourselves.
3. When we asked, the staff said the doctor was eating and we were late. I'm very confused. They are service staff, why didn't they tell the customer? They didn't apologize and even spoke rudely.
4. Does the doctor have no compassion at all? Okay, we were 10 minutes late, but changing orthodontic rubber bands only takes 5 minutes. They do it very quickly and efficiently. Normally, it doesn't take that long. But making the patient sit and wait while the doctor eats is confusing enough, but I'm still trying to understand because we were late. The second thing that confuses me is that they ate without being able to tell us what time they would be eating. We think this is unacceptable.
And when we were talking to the staff in front of the doctor's room, they were right there and heard everything. But they didn't seem to care to say anything; they seemed okay with the staff speaking to us like that.

*** P.S. Another doctor here is lovely, her name is Dr. Luknam. She's kind and speaks nicely; I met her once. But the doctor in charge of my case is usually like this, making patients wait to eat first, and she's very heavy-handed in my opinion.
